newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bids to lift gloom with free ice shows.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bids to lift gloom with free ice shows.

text.p: New York has done it for years. Now Belgium's capital, bidding to improve its international image and give people a little fun, has set up an outdoor ice ring in its famed baroque central square.

"This is a spectacular event which will be very good for promoting the image of Brussels as a centre of culture, of tourism and to give people some joy at the end of the year," Brussels Mayor Francois-Xavier de Donnea told Reuters on Friday.
The 800 square metre (yard) ice rink that takes up some two-thirds of Grand Place will operate until January 5.
One hour's skating -- including hire of skates -- costs 100 francs ($3). The rink can take up to 300 skaters at a time.
In between the public sessions there will be ice spectaculars, starting on Friday night with Moscow on Ice, a five-act ballet lasting just over two hours.

There will also be curling competitions, a ball broom (ice hockey played with brooms instead of sticks) match between Belgium and Canada, figure skating shows, speed skating demonstrations, Father Christmas on ice and a New Year special.
"This is not costing the tax payer anything," de Donnea said. "Everything has been paid for by the sponsors."
The project, which if successful will become an annual event, has taken 18 months to plan.

But according to de Donnea, the timing could not have been better with Belgium's international image badly battered by more than four months of revelations of paedophile abuse and murder and political scandals causing a collapse of public confidence.
"There is a lack of confidence, a sadness, a depression in Belgium. I hope that this spectacle can give some cheer to people," he said.
"I also hope it can do a little bit to counteract the bad image we have had in other countries because of what has happened in the past few months."
"What has happened...is only a tiny part of Belgium. I hope that this will help to show that we are a creative and cultured people," he said.

In front of the ice rink stands a tall pine tree donated to Brussels by Finland. At its foot, attached to white flowers, are the pictures of the four young girls who have been found dead since mid-August -- victims of a child abduction, and sexual abuse gang led by convicted rapist Marc Dutroux.
